decisions.title: Adopt the 0.85.1 host release without a local adapter
decisions.rationale: Grade: Adopt. Reversibility: Tier 1 package rollback and reviewed-baseline edit. Bottom line: accept the installed Pi 0.85.1 behavior without ce-workflow source changes. Verified project fit: model selection is registry-driven, compaction and lifecycle use public host APIs, and ce-workflow does not own the affected SDK-session, native-tool, provider-wire, or custom-editor layers. Verified upstream evidence: the installed 0.85.1 changelog, package metadata, public model documentation, and captured 0.84.4-to-0.85.1 artifact document GPT-6 Astra, native-tool cwd, compaction cancellation, Claude effort, provider streaming, session, and TUI fixes. Benefit: inherit the release improvements without duplicate code. Cost/risk: ordinary host regression exposure and separately required model authentication. Confidence: high. Recommendation: adopt now and keep the current public-API integrations.

decisions.title: Verified private workflow generation
decisions.rationale: The official stable release is translated into the complete private nine-workflow generation with no ordinary CE runtime surface.

decisions.title: Use the native supervisor reply channel
decisions.rationale: Grade: Adopt. Reversibility: Tier 1 prompt and policy change. Bottom line: answer child contact_supervisor requests through subagent_supervisor and keep intercom only for optional peer coordination. Verified project fit: ce roles use contact_supervisor, while the parent policy incorrectly directed replies through external intercom. Verified upstream evidence: the installed 0.66.0 changelog and configuration documentation pair contact_supervisor with the native subagent_supervisor control. Benefit: blocked children receive answers through the supported path without an optional bridge. Cost/risk: small wording and assertion changes while preserving stale-request checks. Confidence: high. Recommendation: use native supervisor control for child requests.
decisions.verification: node scripts/test-work-goal.mjs; LSP diagnostics clean for extensions/work-models.ts and scripts/test-work-goal.mjs

decisions.title: Validate the native-session async migration
decisions.rationale: Grade: Trial. Reversibility: Tier 0 operational smoke test. Bottom line: validate the 0.65 native-session migration and 0.66 completion fixes with a bounded read-only async workflow before accepting them. Verified project fit: ce launches async roles with durable run identity, output, attention, and terminal-state reconciliation. Verified upstream evidence: the installed changelog and agent/observability docs describe native AgentSession children and repaired result/completion publication. Benefit: confirms the installed Pi and plugin combination preserves terminal results and artifacts. Cost/risk: one read-only run. Confidence: medium-high. Recommendation: accept the migration after one successful async completion.
decisions.verification: Async workflow e3e320a8-cf20-4d45-8444-df54212e3660 completed all three read-only children; its workflow receipt reports complete with three completed terminal states and retained transcripts

decisions.title: Keep specialist routing coded and the RPC launch boundary unchanged
decisions.rationale: Grade: Reject. Reversibility: Tier 1 prompt/catalog policy. Bottom line: do not advertise ce specialists into the parent prompt or add alias configuration without an observed provider mismatch. Verified project fit: ce already selects narrow roles deterministically and launches validated RPC workflows with stable identities; no requested-versus-returned model mismatch exists. Verified upstream evidence: 0.66 documents optional agent advertisement, response aliases, and named trusted workflow resources rather than requirements for existing RPC consumers. Benefit: avoids prompt bloat, accidental gate bypass, and identity masking. Cost/risk: operators retain manual configuration for a future evidenced mismatch. Confidence: high. Recommendation: keep the current coded routing and fail-closed identity checks.

decisions.title: Package-owned native sessions and workflow resources
decisions.rationale: Grade: Not-our-problem. Reversibility: Tier 2 execution-interface architecture. Bottom line: inherit native sessions, completion delivery, ambient extension loading, and trusted named workflow resources from pi-subagents without creating a second ce execution surface. Verified project fit: ce owns its validated RPC inline workflow, leases, and recovery policy and does not register trusted host-command workflows. Verified upstream evidence: the installed 0.66.0 changelog, extension API, agent, workflow, and observability docs plus the captured 0.64.0-to-0.66.0 artifact document these package-owned capabilities. Benefit: reliability arrives from the plugin owner. Cost/risk: ordinary upstream regression exposure. Confidence: high. Recommendation: keep the current launch interface.

decisions.title: Package-owned private outcome events and compatibility fixes
decisions.rationale: Grade: Not-our-problem. Reversibility: Tier 1 package rollback. Bottom line: inherit redacted ask outcome events, Kitty repeat/release filtering, and TypeBox-shim compatibility directly from pi-ask-user. Verified project fit: ce-workflow consumes ask_user through normal tool results and lifecycle hooks, has no ask:answered or ask:cancelled listener, does not set PI_ASK_USER_EMIT_FULL_EVENTS, and does not copy the plugin schema or overlay listener. Verified upstream evidence: the installed 0.15.0 README, package metadata, public schema, implementation diff, and captured 0.14.0-to-0.15.0 artifact document these surfaces; the package ships no changelog. Benefit: safer event privacy and more reliable prompts without a second owner. Cost/risk: ordinary upstream regression exposure. Confidence: high. Recommendation: no local event adapter or full-event opt-in.

decisions.title: Open ask_user decision context by default
decisions.rationale: Grade: Adopt. Reversibility: Tier 1 environment default. Bottom line: set PI_ASK_USER_CONTEXT_EXPANDED=true when ce-workflow loads so decision evidence is visible without Ctrl+E. Verified project fit: ce-workflow routinely supplies decision context for planning, approvals, and recovery; the extension-level default covers every ask_user call while preserving an explicit true or false user environment preference. Verified upstream evidence: pi-ask-user 0.15.0 reads PI_ASK_USER_CONTEXT_EXPANDED at call time and supports contextExpanded as the per-call override. Benefit: actors see the full message immediately. Cost/risk: large contexts consume more terminal space. Confidence: high. Recommendation: use expanded context as ce-workflow's default.

decisions.title: Package-owned session alias command and Unicode-safe Windows broker launch
decisions.rationale: Grade: Not-our-problem. Reversibility: Tier 1 package rollback. Bottom line: inherit the /alias command and UTF-16LE Windows hidden-launcher fix from pi-intercom without a ce-workflow adapter. Verified project fit: ce-workflow does not name sessions or spawn the intercom broker, keeps pi-intercom optional, uses list-cwd only for operator discovery, and already requires exact session IDs for trust-sensitive or ambiguous coordination. Verified upstream evidence: the installed 0.13.0 README, package metadata, implementation diff, public command/tool behavior, and captured 0.12.1-to-0.13.0 artifact document both changes; the package ships no changelog. Benefit: users can persist a peer-friendly session name and Windows installations with non-ASCII paths launch reliably, while transport ownership stays in the plugin. Cost/risk: ordinary upstream regression exposure. Confidence: high. Recommendation: no local code, docs, or naming convention.

decisions.title: Name ce-workflow role sessions through /alias
decisions.rationale: Grade: Reject. Reversibility: Tier 1 optional naming policy. Bottom line: do not add alias mutation to coded role launches. Verified project fit: managed subagents already carry stable run and child identity, while delayed supervisor guidance intentionally prefers exact session IDs when identity matters. Verified upstream evidence: 0.13.0 presents /alias as a user-facing current-session command, not a subagent routing requirement. Benefit: preserves collision-resistant run identity and avoids persistent name churn. Cost/risk: operators may still set friendly aliases manually for long-lived peer sessions. Confidence: high. Recommendation: reserve /alias for user-managed peers.

decisions.title: Package-owned Markdown completion rendering and metadata refresh
decisions.rationale: Grade: Not-our-problem. Reversibility: Tier 1 package rollback. Bottom line: inherit pi-goal's Markdown rendering for accepted goal_complete results and its package/documentation refresh without a compatibility adapter. Verified project fit: ce-workflow's narrow coexistence path reads the unchanged goal-state session entry and forwards the unchanged public /goal pause and /goal resume commands; it does not render pi-goal tool results or import pi-goal internals. Verified upstream evidence: the installed 0.54.4 source, README, package metadata, and captured 0.54.3-to-0.54.4 artifact show one runtime behavior change confined to goal_complete renderResult, removal of unused piExtension lifecycle metadata, dev-dependency updates, and documentation clarification. Benefit: pi-goal users receive a readable completion card while ce-workflow coexistence stays stable. Cost/risk: ordinary upstream regression exposure. Confidence: high. Recommendation: no local adapter.

decisions.title: Copy pi-goal's completion renderer into work_goal_complete
decisions.rationale: Grade: Reject. Reversibility: Tier 2 tool-rendering and dependency change. Bottom line: do not add a second completion card for ce-workflow's internal terminal tool. Verified project fit: work_goal_complete already returns a bounded completion result and explicitly asks the agent to give the user one concise final summary; work-models.ts currently needs no direct pi-tui import. Verified upstream evidence: 0.54.4's new renderer is scoped to pi-goal's own goal_complete result and introduces Markdown plus theme dependencies. Benefit: avoids duplicate user-visible completion output and a new direct TUI dependency. Cost/risk: the internal tool row remains plain text before the final assistant summary. Confidence: high. Recommendation: retain the existing final-response handoff.

decisions.title: Adopt the 4.1.4 ambient diagnostics release
decisions.rationale: Grade: Adopt. Reversibility: Tier 1 package rollback and reviewed-baseline edit. Bottom line: adopt installed pi-lens 4.1.4 without a ce-workflow source adapter. Verified project fit: the only dedicated integration remains optional read-only project_report orientation, while immutable verifier evidence stays checkpoint-scoped. Verified upstream evidence: installed metadata, changelog, public usage/configuration docs, and the captured 4.1.3-to-4.1.4 artifact document bounded stale-work handling, deferred warning delivery, mutation observation, config provenance, and lifecycle fixes. Benefit: inherit safer diagnostics and test delivery. Cost/risk: ambient lifecycle behavior can expose third-party writes or delayed test entries. Confidence: high. Recommendation: adopt now and preserve the current integration boundary.
decisions.verification: pi-lens mode=all diagnostics ran on the changed implementation/test/policy paths; no blocking finding or unexpected repository mutation occurred; .pi-lens.json remains absent

decisions.title: Keep immutable verifiers checkpoint-only
decisions.rationale: Grade: Reject. Reversibility: Tier 2 role-contract change. Bottom line: do not add effective_config, diagnostics, or live symbol tools to durable verifier allowlists. Verified project fit: the verifier adapter permits exactly the four checkpoint tools and the optional lens role already treats project_report only as orientation. Verified upstream evidence: 4.1.4's new effective_config surface is live workspace provenance, not immutable checkpoint evidence. Benefit: preserves time-of-check guarantees and role availability without optional ambient tools. Cost/risk: config explanation remains an operator diagnostic. Confidence: high. Recommendation: retain the checkpoint-only evidence boundary.

decisions.title: Validate observed-mutation and settled diagnostic delivery
decisions.rationale: Grade: Trial. Reversibility: Tier 1 ambient-package rollback or autofix disablement. Bottom line: exercise one bounded real diagnostics run and require a clean post-run repository state before accepting the new mutation and settlement behavior. Verified project fit: ce completion gates already guard formatter/autofix expansion and unexpected dirt. Verified upstream evidence: 4.1.4 observes unknown mutating tools through a bounded bridge and delays test-failure delivery until host-confirmed settlement. Benefit: catches otherwise invisible writes without weakening completion gates. Cost/risk: deferred diagnostics could appear near finish gates. Confidence: medium. Recommendation: accept after one clean bounded run.
decisions.verification: lens_diagnostics mode=all completed on the changed paths; subsequent git status matched the known pre-run plus intentional catch-up edits, and no project pi-lens config was created

decisions.title: Do not bootstrap project pi-lens configuration
decisions.rationale: Grade: Not-our-problem. Reversibility: Tier 1 conditional configuration. Bottom line: keep the existing rule not to create a project config when none exists. Verified project fit: this repository has no .pi-lens.json or .pi-lens directory and worker policy already handles configuration conditionally. Verified upstream evidence: 4.1.4 provides redacted effective_config provenance and stable PILENS_CFG notices for real migrations. Benefit: avoids imposing repo-wide LSP/mutation policy without an observed warning. Cost/risk: a future warning still requires targeted migration evidence. Confidence: high. Recommendation: migrate only after a current config notice and provenance result.
